cards.text: Friend, it's early on the first day of the week, and it's still dark. Jesus has been laid in a new tomb in a garden, near where He was crucified (John 19:41-42). Mary Magdalene, who stood near His cross (John 19:25), heads out to that tomb.

cards.question: Mary Magdalene reaches the tomb while it's still dark. What does she see at the entrance?

answers.text: The stone is still in place

cards.text: So Mary RUNS. No streetlights, no phone flashlight, just RUNNING, straight to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved.

cards.question: Mary tells Peter and the other disciple that she knows where the Lord's body has been put.

cards.text: Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb, running together. Two grown men in a full sprint, friend. This is a RACE now.

cards.question: Peter and the other disciple are running together to the tomb. Who gets there first?

cards.text: First place goes to the other disciple, and I respect it, because I hop everywhere on this gold base and I have never won a race in my LIFE. He bends down and looks in at the linen cloths lying there.

cards.question: After looking in at the linen cloths, the other disciple goes right inside the tomb.

cards.text: Then here comes Simon Peter, just after him, and Peter does NOT stop at the door. Second place in the race, first one inside, and he sees the linen cloths lying there.

cards.question: Peter also sees the cloth that had been around Jesus' ___, rolled up and lying ___ from the linen cloths.

cards.text: Then the other disciple, the one who got there first, finally goes in too.

cards.question: The other disciple stands inside the tomb and sees it all. How does he respond?
At this point, Peter and the other disciple already understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.

cards.text: Then the disciples return to their homes. Empty tomb, rolled-up cloth, and they just go HOME? I'd still be in there interviewing the cloth.
But Mary doesn't go anywhere. She stands outside the tomb weeping, and as she weeps, she bends down to look inside.

cards.question: Mary Magdalene bends down and looks into the tomb. Who does she see?
The two angels are sitting where Jesus' body had lain, one at the ___ and the other at the ___.

cards.text: The angels ask her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” Two angels in white, friend. If that were me, I'd have dropped every cookie box in the bakery.

cards.question: The angels ask Mary why she's weeping. What does she tell them?

answers.text: Someone has taken her Lord away
She came too late for the burial
The disciples have left her alone

cards.text: Mary says this, and then she turns around and sees Jesus standing there.

cards.question: Mary recognizes Jesus the moment she turns around and sees Him.

cards.text: Jesus asks her the same question the angels asked: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Then He adds, “Whom are you seeking?”

cards.question: Mary still doesn't know it's Jesus. In that garden, she thinks He is the ___.

cards.text: She says, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.” She's offering to go get Him herself, friend, and I can't carry one cookie box without my mustache doing ALL the work.
Then Jesus says just one word. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer with nobody saying my name, so trust me, a name hits DIFFERENT.

cards.question: Jesus says just one word to Mary. What is it?
Mary turns and says to Jesus in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” which means ___.

cards.text: One word, her name, and she knows Him. Jesus tells her, “Do not cling to Me,” because He has not yet ascended to the Father.

cards.question: Jesus tells Mary not to cling to Him. What does He send her to do?

answers.text: Keep it a secret for now

cards.question: Jesus gives Mary a message for His brothers: He is ascending to His Father and their Father, to His God and their God.

cards.text: So Mary Magdalene goes to the disciples, and this time she's not bringing “They have taken the Lord.” Oh no, friend. This time is DIFFERENT.

cards.question: Mary Magdalene goes to the disciples with an announcement. What does she tell them?

answers.text: The gardener knows where He is

cards.text: And she tells them what He said to her. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but this first day of the week is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "They have taken the Lord.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb, running together." / "Two grown men in a full sprint, friend." / "This is a RACE now." Only the opening card can run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The second blank gives away its answer. Of the five words, only "separate" and "together" can fit "lying ___ from the linen cloths." "Together from" isn't grammatical, so "separate" is the only word that fits.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: "Finally goes in too" makes the wait sound long. John 20:8 says only "Then the other disciple... also went in," with no time given.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Then the disciples return to their homes." / "Empty tomb, rolled-up cloth, and they just go HOME?" / "I'd still be in there interviewing the cloth."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Peter and the other disciple" is ruled out by the card just before it (stop 1, card 14), which says the disciples went home. A thoughtful baker can drop it without knowing the answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question gives the answer away: "In that garden, she thinks He is the ___" makes "gardener" stand out from "guard" and "priest" because of the wording, not because the baker reasoned it out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Mary offers to carry the body herself. Papa Dorin's mustache is his hands, so "I can't carry one cookie box without my mustache doing ALL the work" is like saying he needs his hands to carry things. There's no real comparison, and it falls flat in a moment of grief.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The joke "a name hits DIFFERENT" tells the baker that the one word Jesus says is a name. That gives away the answer to card 12 ("Mary" versus "Peace" and "Rise").

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "This time she's not bringing 'They have taken the Lord'... This time is DIFFERENT" tells the baker the news is no longer about a missing body. That rules out the wrong answers on card 18 ("The angels have His body" and "The gardener knows where He is").

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "So Mary Magdalene goes to the disciples, and this time she's not bringing 'They have taken the Lord.'" / "Oh no, friend." / "This time is DIFFERENT."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line reuses the doc's example wording: "That's where we'll leave it for now, friend" copies "And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend..."

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
